{{Short description|Chinese mathematician (born 1982)}}
{{Western name order|Zhu Xinwen}}

[[File:Xinwen Zhu (Oberwolfach 2015).jpg|thumb|right|Zhu in 2015]]

'''Xinwen Zhu''' ({{zh|c=朱歆文}}; born 1982 in [[Sichuan]]) is a Chinese mathematician and professor at [[Stanford University]]. His work deals primarily with geometric representation theory and in particular the [[Langlands program]], tying [[number theory]] to [[algebraic geometry]] and [[quantum physics]].<ref name="CaltechInterview">[https://www.caltech.edu/news/prime-numbers-quantum-fields-and-donuts-interview-xinwen-zhu-45000 "Prime Numbers, Quantum Fields, and Donuts: An Interview with Xinwen Zhu"], ''[[Caltech]]''. Retrieved on 3 December 2016.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pku.org.cn/?p=25929|script-title=zh:北大数学校友创新合作: 统一数论与几何|trans-title=New collaboration among Peking University mathematics alumni: unifying number theory and geometry|publisher=Peking University|date=15 December 2015|access-date=7 August 2017}}</ref>

==Biography==
Zhu obtained his A.B. in mathematics from [[Peking University]] in 2004 and his Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 2009 under the direction of [[Edward Frenkel]].<ref name="CaltechInterview"/> He taught at [[Harvard University]] as a Benjamin Peirce Lecturer and at [[Northwestern University]] as an assistant professor before joining the Caltech faculty in 2014. According to the [[American Mathematical Society]], "[Zhu] studies the geometry and topology of flag varieties of loop groups and applies techniques from the geometric Langlands program to arithmetic geometry."<ref>[http://www.ams.org/notices/201306/rnoti-p765.pdf "Mathematics People"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129021059/http://www.ams.org/notices/201306/rnoti-p765.pdf |date=2020-11-29 }}, ''[[Notices of the AMS]]''. Retrieved on 3 December 2016.</ref>

The awards Zhu has received include an [[AMS Centennial Fellowship]] in 2013 and a [[Sloan Fellowship]] in 2015.<ref>[https://www.pma.caltech.edu/content/caltech-professors-awarded-2015-sloan-fellowships "Caltech Professors Awarded 2015 Sloan Fellowships"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170929071530/https://www.pma.caltech.edu/content/caltech-professors-awarded-2015-sloan-fellowships |date=2017-09-29 }}, ''[[Caltech]]''. Retrieved on 3 December 2016.</ref> His research has been published in [[Annals of Mathematics]] and [[Inventiones mathematicae]], among other mathematics journals. Zhu, [[Wei Zhang (mathematician)|Wei Zhang]], [[Xinyi Yuan]] and [[Zhiwei Yun]] are frequent collaborators.<ref>[https://www.quantamagazine.org/20151208-four-mathematicians/ "Math Quartet Joins Forces on Unified Theory"], ''[[Quanta Magazine]]''. Retrieved on 3 December 2016.</ref> In 2019 he received the [[Morningside Medal]] jointly with [[Zhiwei Yun]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/content/show/92-246.html |title=Morningside Medal 2019 |access-date=2019-08-26 |archive-date=2019-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190826095759/http://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/content/show/92-246.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Zhu won the 2020 New Horizons in Mathematics [[Breakthrough Prize]] "For work in arithmetic algebraic geometry including applications to the theory of Shimura varieties and the Riemann-Hilbert problem for p-adic varieties."

== Publications (selected) ==
* (with [[Edward Frenkel]]) [http://imrn.oxfordjournals.org/content/2012/17/3929.short "Gerbal Representations of Double Loop Groups"], [[International Mathematics Research Notices]] 2012 (2012), No. 17, 3929–4013.
* (with George Pappas]) [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00222-012-0442-z "Local models of Shimura varieties and a conjecture of Kottwitz"], [[Inventiones mathematicae]] 194 (2013), No. 1, 147–254.
* [https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2014/180-1/p01 "On the coherence conjecture of Pappas and Rapoport"], [[Annals of Mathematics]] 180 (2014), No. 1, 1–85.
* (with Denis Osipov) [https://msp.org/ant/2011/5-3/ant-v5-n3-p01-p.pdf "A categorical proof of the Parshin reciprocity laws on algebraic surfaces"], [[Algebra & Number Theory]] 5 (2011), No. 3, 289–337.
* [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0001870809000140 "Affine Demazure modules and T-fixed point subschemes in the affine Grassmannian"], [[Advances in Mathematics]] 221 (2009), No. 2, 570–600.
* [http://annals.math.princeton.edu/articles/10026 "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220050958/http://annals.math.princeton.edu/articles/10026 |date=2016-12-20 }}, [[Annals of Mathematics]] 185 (2017), No. 2, 403–492.
* (with [[Edward Frenkel]]) [https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.3186 "Any flat bundle on a punctured disc has an oper structure"], Mathematical Research Letters 17 (2010), no. 1, 27–37. 
* [https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.5762 "The geometric Satake correspondence for ramified groups"], [[Annales Scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure]] 48 (2015), no. 2, 409–451.
* (with [[Zhiwei Yun]]) [https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.5487 "Integral homology of loop groups via Langlands dual groups"], Representation Theory 15 (2011), 347–369.
* (with An Huang, Bong H. Lian) [https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jdg/1476367060 "Period integrals and the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence"], [[Journal of Differential Geometry]] 104 (2016), No. 2, 325–369.
* (with Tsao-Hsien Chen) [https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.3981 "Geometric Langlands in prime characteristic"], [[Compositio Mathematica]] 153 (2017), No. 2, 395–452.
